title: Specialization of a relative associated point at a flat fibre-component generic point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. For $s\in S$ let $X_s$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $i_s:X_s\to X$ its projection and $\mathcal F_s=i_s^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. A point $x\in X_s$ is an associated point of $\mathcal F_s$ if the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is an associated prime [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes] of the stalk $(\mathcal F_s)_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] as an $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$-module. The relative assassin $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ is the set of points $x\in X$ which, regarded as points of $X_{f(x)}$, are associated points of $\mathcal F_{f(x)}$. $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at $x\in X$ if the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is a flat $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$-module [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Let $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and put $t=f(y)$. Let $Y=\overline{\{y\}}\subseteq X$ with its reduced integral closed-subscheme structure [def-pc-integral-scheme]. For $s\in S$, let $Y_s$ denote the fibre of the composite $Y\to X\to S$. Let $C$ be an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y_s$, and let $x$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point], viewed as a point of $X$. Assume only that $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at this point $x$. Then $x\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and $\dim_x(Y_s)=\dim C=\dim(Y_t)$, where $\dim$ is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $\dim_x$ is local topological dimension [def-kun-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), statement and proof, second paragraph: the equality of the dimension of C with that of C′ and Y_t.

proof.text: The integral closed subscheme $Y\hookrightarrow X$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2), so $Y\to S$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). These assertions remain true after arbitrary base change by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], and hold also for the integral closed subschemes $Y'$ used below. In particular all fibres and field-extended fibres used below are locally of finite type over their fields, hence locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the whole field. No Noetherianity of $S$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, preparations for the fibre and local-ring arguments; Morphisms Tags 01T5, 01T6, 01T9, 01T0

proof.text: For each of these locally algebraic fibres, at a component generic point $z$ one has $\dim_z Z=\dim\overline{\{z\}}$. Indeed [lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite] gives a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many components; remove the other components, none of which contains $z$, to obtain an open neighbourhood contained in its component $D$. On this neighbourhood the ambient space and $D$ have the same topology. [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] gives $\dim_zD=\dim D$, proving the assertion from the neighbourhood definition of dimension. Apply this in particular to $x\in Y_s$ to obtain $\dim_xY_s=\dim C$. Also $Y_t$ is irreducible with generic point $y$: on affine charts it is obtained from the domain defining $Y$ by inverting the nonzero functions on the integral image closure of $t$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, second paragraph and the interpretation of the displayed local dimension; Varieties Tag 0A21(3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuative-fibre-component-lift] to $f,y,s,x$. Retain its square $X'=X\times_SS'$, valuation base $S'=\operatorname{Spec}A$, points $t',s',y',x'$ and integral closed subscheme $Y'=\overline{\{y'\}}$. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$. Write $C'$ for the component of $Y'_{s'}$ with generic point $x'$. The generic fibre $Y'_{t'}$ is the component of $Y_t\times_t t'$ with generic point $y'$: on affine charts taking the prime defining the closure of $y'$ and then localizing in $A\setminus\{0\}$ recovers the prime of that component.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, first paragraph: choose the diagram of Tag 0GSH

proof.text: Put $\mathcal F'=(g')^*\mathcal F$. It is quasi-coherent and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type]. The stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] and pointwise scalar extension [lem-pc-pullback-stalk-relative-flat-extension], applied with $M=\mathcal F_x$, give that $\mathcal F'_{x'}$ is $A$-flat; here $\mathcal O_{S',s'}=A$. Since $y'$ is generic in a component of $Y_t\times_t t'$, it is generic in its fibre over the generic point $y$ (localizing at $y$ preserves minimal primes). The residual fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(t')\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(y))$. As $y$ is relatively associated, [lem-trf-relative-assassin-base-change] therefore gives $y'\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal F')$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, first paragraph: relative assassin base change (05DC) and pointwise flat base change (01U8)

proof.text: Prove $x'\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal F')$ by contradiction. Set $B=\mathcal O_{X',x'}$, $N=\mathcal F'_{x'}$, $R=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ and $L=N/\mathfrak m_AN$. Choose a finite type affine $A$-chart around $x'$ and an affine module presentation there. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], $B$ is a localization at a prime of that finite type algebra and $N$ is a finite $B$-module. The local map $A\to B$ is thus essentially of finite type. The same localization formulas on the closed-fibre chart and [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] identify $R=\mathcal O_{X'_{s'},x'}$ and $L=(\mathcal F'_{s'})_{x'}$. Thus $R$ is Noetherian by step 1 and $L$ is finite. If $x'$ is not relatively associated, the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$ is not associated to $L$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, third paragraph: local algebra A to B, finite module N, and closed-fibre stalks

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be the prime corresponding to $y'$, which specializes to $x'$. In the local spectrum the closure of $y'$ is $V(\mathfrak q)$. Its closed fibre at $x'$ has just one prime, since $x'$ is the generic point of its fibre component and localization keeps only primes contained in $\mathfrak m_B$. Consequently $\sqrt{\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_AB}=\mathfrak m_B$, or $\sqrt{\overline{\mathfrak q}}=\mathfrak m_R$ for the image ideal in $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] to the Noetherian local ring $R$ and finite module $L$: obtain $h\in\mathfrak m_R$ acting injectively on $L$. Some power $h^n$, with $n\ge1$, lies in $\overline{\mathfrak q}$, so choose $g\in\mathfrak q$ with image $h^n$ in $R$. Its multiplication on $L$ is injective as a composite of $n$ injective maps. This is the source's prime-avoidance conclusion, obtained here from the existing nonzerodivisor lemma and the radical equality.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, third paragraph: radical equality and choice of g (prime-avoidance conclusion)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-finite-module-injectivity] to multiplication $g:N\to N$. The two $B$-modules are finite, the target is $A$-flat by step 4, the map $A\to B$ is local essentially of finite type, and its reduction is injective by step 6. Hence $g$ acts injectively on $N$. It remains injective after both localizations used to reach the generic-fibre stalk at $y'$: if $g(n/u)=0$, the fraction criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] supplies a further denominator $v$ with $vgn=0$; injectivity gives $vn=0$ and thus $n/u=0$. By the affine stalk and pullback formulas of step 5, this localized module is $(\mathcal F'_{t'})_{y'}$, over $(B\otimes_AK)_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{X'_{t'},y'}$. But $y'$ is relatively associated, so this stalk has a nonzero element annihilated by its maximal ideal. The element $g\in\mathfrak q$ maps into that maximal ideal and kills it, contradicting injectivity. Therefore $x'$ is relatively associated.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, third paragraph: injectivity lifted using 0GSG and contradiction on the generic-fibre stalk

proof.text: By [lem-trf-relative-assassin-base-change], the associated point $x'$ maps to $x\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and is generic in the residue-field fibre over $x$ of $X'_{s'}\to X_s$. This same residual fibre occurs for $Y_s\times_s s'\to Y_s$, since $x\in Y_s$ and a closed immersion does not change its residue field. Because $x$ is a component generic point of $Y_s$, $x'$ is a component generic point of $Y_s\times_s s'$: on affine charts, a prime properly contained in the prime of $x'$ would contract to a prime contained in the minimal prime of $x$, hence to that same prime; after localizing at $x$ it would contradict minimality in the residue-field fibre. Thus the closure of $x'$ in $Y_s\times_s s'$ is an irreducible component. It equals $C'$ topologically because $Y'_{s'}$ is a closed subscheme of this base change and contains $x'$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, second paragraph: descend association and identify the special component after field extension

proof.text: Choose a finite type affine $A$-chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}D\subset Y'$ containing $x'$. Its coordinate ring is a domain and $A\to D$ is injective: every nonempty open of the integral scheme $Y'$ contains $y'$, whose image is the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so a nonzero element of $A$ cannot vanish in $D$. The fibre $W_{s'}$ is nonempty. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-domain-fibre-dimensions]: every component of $W_{s'}$ has dimension $\dim(D\otimes_AK)$. In particular $C'\cap W$ is such a component by [lem-sc-components-open-injection]. By [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic], its dimension is $\dim C'$, while the nonempty open $W_{t'}$ of the irreducible $Y'_{t'}$ has dimension $\dim Y'_{t'}$. The affine spectrum/ring comparison [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] identifies $\dim W_{t'}=\dim(D\otimes_AK)$. Hence $\dim C'=\dim Y'_{t'}$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI, first paragraph: apply Algebra Tag 00QK on an affine neighbourhood of x′

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to $Y\to S$ at $y'$ over $t'$: $\dim_{y'}(Y_t\times_t t')=\dim_yY_t$. Step 2 identifies the left side with $\dim Y'_{t'}$ and the right side with $\dim Y_t$, since $y'$ is generic in its component and $Y_t$ is irreducible. The same base-change lemma at $x'$ over $s'$ gives $\dim_{x'}(Y_s\times_s s')=\dim_xY_s$. By step 8, $x'$ is a component generic point of this entire base change, so step 2 identifies its local dimension with $\dim C'$. Combining these equalities with steps 2 and 9 gives $\dim_xY_s=\dim C=\dim C'=\dim Y'_{t'}=\dim Y_t$. Together with step 8 this is the required conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem flat_relative_associated_specialization {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (y : X) (hy : y ∈ Scheme.Modules.relativeAssassin f F) (s : S) (C : Set ((f.associatedPointClosureToBase y).fiber s)) (hC : C ∈ irreducibleComponents ((f.associatedPointClosureToBase y).fiber s)) (x : (f.associatedPointClosureToBase y).fiber s) (hx : IsGenericPoint x C) (hflat : Module.Flat (S.presheaf.stalk (f (f.associatedPointClosureFiberToAmbient y s x))) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (f.stalkMap (f.associatedPointClosureFiberToAmbient y s x)).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (f.associatedPointClosureFiberToAmbient y s x)).obj F))) : f.associatedPointClosureFiberToAmbient y s x ∈ Scheme.Modules.relativeAssassin f F ∧ topologicalKrullDimAt x = topologicalKrullDim C ∧ topologicalKrullDim C = topologicalKrullDim ((f.associatedPointClosureToBase y).fiber (f y))
